trs.20: By the star when it descends,
trs.85: By the star when it sets!
trs.22: By the Star when it goes down,-
trs.203: By the star when it goes down (or vanishes).

trs.20: Your companion [i.e., Muḥammad] has not strayed, nor has he erred,
trs.85: Your companion has not strayed; he is not deluded;
trs.22: Your Companion is neither astray nor being misled.
trs.203: Your companion (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) has neither gone astray nor has erred.

trs.20: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination.
trs.85: he does not speak from his own desire.
trs.22: Nor does he say (aught) of (his own) Desire.
trs.203: Nor does he speak of (his own) desire.

trs.20: It is not but a revelation revealed,
trs.85: The Quran is nothing less than a revelation that is sent to him.
trs.22: It is no less than inspiration sent down to him:
trs.203: It is only a Revelation revealed.

trs.20: Taught to him by one intense in strength [i.e., Gabriel] -
trs.85: It was taught to him by [an angel] with mighty powers
trs.22: He was taught by one Mighty in Power,
trs.203: He has been taught (this Qur’ân) by one mighty in power [Jibrîl (Gabriel)]

trs.20: One of soundness.<sup foot_note=197440>1</sup> And he rose to [his] true form<sup foot_note=197439>2</sup>
trs.85: and great strength, who stood
trs.22: Endued with Wisdom: for he appeared (in stately form);
trs.203: One free from any defect in body and mind then he (Jibrîl - Gabriel in his real shape as created by Allah) rose and became stable.

trs.20: While he was in the higher [part of the] horizon.<sup foot_note=197441>1</sup>
trs.85: on the highest horizon
trs.22: While he was in the highest part of the horizon:
trs.203: While he [Jibrîl (Gabriel)] was in the highest part of the horizon, (Tafsir Ibn Kathir)

trs.20: Then he approached and descended
trs.85: and then approached––coming down
trs.22: Then he approached and came closer,
trs.203: Then he [Jibrîl (Gabriel)] approached and came closer,

trs.20: And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer.
trs.85: until he was two bow-lengths away or even closer––
trs.22: And was at a distance of but two bow-lengths or (even) nearer;
trs.203: And was at a distance of two bows’ length or (even) nearer.

trs.20: And he revealed to His Servant<sup foot_note=197442>1</sup> what he revealed [i.e., conveyed].
trs.85: and revealed to God’s servant what He revealed.
trs.22: So did (Allah) convey the inspiration to His Servant- (conveyed) what He (meant) to convey.
trs.203: So (Allâh) revealed to His slave [Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم through Jibrîl (Gabriel) عليه السلام] whatever He revealed.

trs.20: The heart<sup foot_note=197443>1</sup> did not lie [about] what it saw.
trs.85: [The Prophet’s] own heart did not distort what he saw.
trs.22: The (Prophet's) (mind and) heart in no way falsified that which he saw.
trs.203: The (Prophet’s) heart lied not in what he (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) saw.

trs.20: So will you dispute with him over what he saw?
trs.85: Are you going to dispute with him what he saw with his own eyes?
trs.22: Will ye then dispute with him concerning what he saw?
trs.203: Will you then dispute with him (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) about what he saw [during the Mi‘râj: (Ascent of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم to the seven heavens)]<sup foot_note=154947>1</sup>

translation.text: Then will you dispute with him

trs.20: And he certainly saw him in another descent<sup foot_note=197444>1</sup>
trs.85: A second time he saw him:
trs.22: For indeed he saw him at a second descent,
trs.203: And indeed he (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) saw him [Jibrîl (Gabriel)] at a second descent (i.e. another time).

trs.20: At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary -
trs.85: by the lote tree beyond which none may pass
trs.22: Near the Lote-tree beyond which none may pass:
trs.203: Near Sidrat-ul-Muntaha (a lote-tree of the utmost boundary over the seventh heaven beyond which none can pass).

trs.20: Near it is the Garden of Refuge [i.e., Paradise] -
trs.85: near the Garden of Restfulness,
trs.22: Near it is the Garden of Abode.
trs.203: Near it is the Paradise of Abode.

trs.20: When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered [it].<sup foot_note=197445>1</sup>
trs.85: when the tree was covered in nameless [splendour].
trs.22: Behold, the Lote-tree was shrouded (in mystery unspeakable!)
trs.203: When that covered the lote-tree which did cover it!<sup foot_note=154948>1</sup>

trs.20: The sight [of the Prophet (ﷺ)] did not swerve, nor did it transgress [its limit].
trs.85: His sight never wavered, nor was it too bold,
trs.22: (His) sight never swerved, nor did it go wrong!
trs.203: The sight (of Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) turned not aside (right or left), nor it transgressed beyond the limit (ordained for it).

verses.text_uthmani: لَقَدْ رَأَىٰ مِنْ ءَايَـٰتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰٓ

trs.20: He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord.
trs.85: and he saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord.
trs.22: For truly did he see, of the Signs of his Lord, the Greatest!
trs.203: Indeed he (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) did see of the Greatest Signs, of his Lord (Allâh).

trs.20: So have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā?
trs.85: [Disbelievers], consider al-Lat and al-Uzza,
trs.22: Have ye seen Lat. and 'Uzza,
trs.203: Have you then considered Al-Lât, and Al-‘Uzzâ (two idols of the pagan Arabs)<sup foot_note=154949>1</sup>

trs.20: And Manāt, the third - the other one?<sup foot_note=197446>1</sup>
trs.85: and the third one, Manat––
trs.22: And another, the third (goddess), Manat?
trs.203: And Manât (another idol of the pagan Arabs), the other third?

trs.20: Is the male for you and for Him the female?
trs.85: are you to have the male and He the female?
trs.22: What! for you the male sex, and for Him, the female?
trs.203: Is it for you the males and for Him the females?

trs.20: That, then, is an unjust division.<sup foot_note=197447>1</sup>
trs.85: That would be a most unjust distribution!––
trs.22: Behold, such would be indeed a division most unfair!
trs.203: That indeed is a division most unfair!

verses.text_uthmani: إِنْ هِىَ إِلَّآ أَسْمَآءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمْ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَـٰنٍ ۚ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى ٱلْأَنفُسُ ۖ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ

trs.20: They are not but [mere] names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allāh has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what [their] souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance.
trs.85: these are nothing but names you have invented yourselves, you and your forefathers. God has sent no authority for them. These people merely follow guesswork and the whims of their souls, even though guidance has come to them from their Lord.
trs.22: These are nothing but names which ye have devised,- ye and your fathers,- for which Allah has sent down no authority (whatever). They follow nothing but conjecture and what their own souls desire!- Even though there has already come to them Guidance from their Lord!
trs.203: They are but names which you have named - you and your fathers - for which Allâh has sent down no authority. They follow but a guess and that which they themselves desire, whereas there has surely come to them the Guidance from their Lord!

trs.20: Or is there for man whatever he wishes?
trs.85: Is man to have everything he wishes for,
trs.22: Nay, shall man have (just) anything he hankers after?
trs.203: Or shall man have what he wishes?

trs.20: Rather, to Allāh belongs the Hereafter and the first [life].
trs.85: when the present life and the life to come belong only to God?
trs.22: But it is to Allah that the End and the Beginning (of all things) belong.
trs.203: But to Allâh belongs the last (Hereafter) and the first (the world).

verses.text_uthmani: ۞ وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكٍ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغْنِى شَفَـٰعَتُهُمْ شَيْـًٔا إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ أَن يَأْذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرْضَىٰٓ

trs.20: And how many angels there are in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except [only] after Allāh has permitted [it] to whom He wills and approves.
trs.85: There are many angels in heaven whose intercession will be of no use until God gives permission to those He will, whose words He will accept.
trs.22: How many-so-ever be the angels in the heavens, their intercession will avail nothing except after Allah has given leave for whom He pleases and that he is acceptable to Him.
trs.203: And there are many angels in the heavens, whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allâh has given leave for whom He wills and is pleased with.

verses.text_uthmani: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ ٱلْأُنثَىٰ

trs.20: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels female names,
trs.85: Those who deny the life to come give the angels female names.
trs.22: Those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names.
trs.203: Verily, those who believe not in the Hereafter, name the angels with female names.

verses.text_uthmani: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ ۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ ۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِى مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ شَيْـًٔا

trs.20: And they have thereof no knowledge. They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all.
trs.85: They have no knowledge to base this on: they merely follow guesswork. Guesswork is of no value against the Truth.
trs.22: But they have no knowledge therein. They follow nothing but conjecture; and conjecture avails nothing against Truth.
trs.203: But they have no knowledge thereof. They follow but a guess, and verily, guess is no substitute for the truth.

verses.text_uthmani: فَأَعْرِضْ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا

trs.20: So turn away from whoever turns his back on Our message and desires not except the worldly life.
trs.85: So [Prophet] ignore those who turn away from Our revelation, who want only the life of this world.
trs.22: Therefore shun those who turn away from Our Message and desire nothing but the life of this world.
trs.203: Therefore withdraw (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) from him who turns away from Our Reminder (this Qur’ân) and desires nothing but the life of this world.

verses.text_uthmani: ذَٰلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُم مِّنَ ٱلْعِلْمِ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهْتَدَىٰ

trs.20: That is their sum of knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided.
trs.85: Their knowledge does not go beyond that. Your Lord knows best who strays from His path and who follows guidance.
trs.22: That is as far as knowledge will reach them. Verily thy Lord knoweth best those who stray from His Path, and He knoweth best those who receive guidance.
trs.203: That is what they could reach of knowledge. Verily, your Lord it is He Who knows best him who goes astray from His Path, and He knows best him who receives guidance.

verses.text_uthmani: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَـٰٓـُٔوا۟ بِمَا عَمِلُوا۟ وَيَجْزِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ بِٱلْحُسْنَى

trs.20: And to Allāh belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth - that He may recompense those who do evil with [the penalty of] what they have done and recompense those who do good with the best [reward] -
trs.85: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God. He will repay those who do evil according to their deeds, and reward, with what is best, those who do good.
trs.22: Yea, to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and on earth: so that He rewards those who do evil, according to their deeds, and He rewards those who do good, with what is best.
trs.203: And to Allâh belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth, that He may requite those who do evil with that which they have done (i.e. punish them in Hell), and reward those who do good, with what is best (i.e. Paradise).

verses.text_uthmani: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَـٰٓئِرَ ٱلْإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلْمَغْفِرَةِ ۚ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِكُمْ ۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ ۖ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ

trs.20: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only [committing] slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him.
trs.85: As for those who avoid grave sins and foul acts, though they may commit small sins, your Lord is ample in forgiveness. He has been aware of you from the time He produced you from the earth and from your hiding places in your mothers’ wombs, so do not assert your own goodness:He knows best who is mindful of Him.
trs.22: Those who avoid great sins and shameful deeds, only (falling into) small faults,- verily thy Lord is ample in forgiveness. He knows you well when He brings you out of the earth, And when ye are hidden in your mothers' wombs. Therefore justify not yourselves: He knows best who it is that guards against evil.
trs.203: Those who avoid great sins (See the Qur’ân, Verses: 6:152,153) and Al-Fawâhish (illegal sexual intercourse) except the small faults, - verily, your Lord is of Vast Forgiveness. He knows you well when He created you from the earth (Adam), and when you were fetuses in your mothers’ wombs. So ascribe not purity to yourselves. He knows best him who fears Allâh and keeps his duty to Him [i.e. those who are Al-Muttaqûn (the pious. See V.2:2)].

trs.20: Have you seen the one who turned away
trs.85: [Prophet], consider that man who turned away:
trs.22: Seest thou one who turns back,
trs.203: Did you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) observe him who turned away (from Islâm).

trs.20: And gave a little and [then] refrained?
trs.85: he only gave a little and then he stopped.
trs.22: Gives a little, then hardens (his heart)?
trs.203: And gave a little, then stopped (giving)?

trs.20: Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees?<sup foot_note=197448>1</sup>
trs.85: Does he have knowledge of the Unseen? Can he see [the Hereafter]?
trs.22: What! Has he knowledge of the Unseen so that he can see?
trs.203: Is with him the knowledge of the Unseen so that he sees?

verses.text_uthmani: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِى صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ

trs.20: Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Moses
trs.85: Has he not been told what was written in the Scriptures of Moses
trs.22: Nay, is he not acquainted with what is in the Books of Moses-
trs.203: Or is he not informed with what is in the Pages (Scripture) of Mûsâ (Moses),

trs.20: And [of] Abraham, who fulfilled [his obligations] -
trs.85: and of Abraham, who fulfilled his duty:
trs.22: And of Abraham who fulfilled his engagements?-
trs.203: And of Ibrâhîm (Abraham) who fulfilled (or conveyed) all that (Allâh ordered him to do or convey):

trs.20: That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another
trs.85: that no soul shall bear the burden of another;
trs.22: Namely, that no bearer of burdens can bear the burden of another;
trs.203: That no burdened person (with sins) shall bear the burden (sins) of another.

verses.text_uthmani: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ

trs.20: And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives
trs.85: that man will only have what he has worked towards;
trs.22: That man can have nothing but what he strives for;
trs.203: And that man can have nothing but what he does (good or bad).<sup foot_note=154950>1</sup>

trs.20: And that his effort is going to be seen -
trs.85: that his labour will be seen
trs.22: That (the fruit of) his striving will soon come in sight:
trs.203: And that his deeds will be seen.

trs.20: Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense -
trs.85: and that in the end he will be repaid in full for it;
trs.22: Then will he be rewarded with a reward complete;
trs.203: Then he will be recompensed with a full and the best recompense.<sup foot_note=154951>1</sup>

translation.text: he will be recompensed for it

trs.20: And that to your Lord is the finality
trs.85: that the final goal is your Lord;
trs.22: That to thy Lord is the final Goal;
trs.203: And that to your Lord (Allâh) is the End (Return of everything).

trs.20: And that it is He who makes [one] laugh and weep
trs.85: that it is He who makes people laugh and weep;
trs.22: That it is He Who granteth Laughter and Tears;
trs.203: And that it is He (Allâh) Who makes (whom He wills) laugh, and makes (whom He wills) weep.

trs.20: And that it is He who causes death and gives life
trs.85: that it is He who gives death and life;
trs.22: That it is He Who granteth Death and Life;
trs.203: And that it is He (Allâh) Who causes death and gives life.

trs.20: And that He creates the two mates - the male and female -
trs.85: that He Himself created the two sexes, male and female,
trs.22: That He did create in pairs,- male and female,
trs.203: And that He (Allâh) creates the pairs, male and female,

trs.20: From a sperm-drop when it is emitted
trs.85: from an ejected drop of sperm;
trs.22: From a seed when lodged (in its place);
trs.203: From Nutfah (drops of semen - male and female discharges) when it is emitted.

trs.20: And that [incumbent] upon Him is the other [i.e., next] creation.
trs.85: that He will undertake the second Creation;
trs.22: That He hath promised a Second Creation (Raising of the Dead);
trs.203: And that upon Him (Allâh) is another bringing forth (Resurrection).

trs.20: And that it is He who enriches and suffices
trs.85: that it is He who gives wealth and possessions;
trs.22: That it is He Who giveth wealth and satisfaction;
trs.203: And that it is He (Allâh) Who gives much or a little (of wealth and contentment)

trs.20: And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius<sup foot_note=197449>1</sup>.
trs.85: that He is the Lord of Sirius;
trs.22: That He is the Lord of Sirius (the Mighty Star);
trs.203: And that He (Allâh) is the Lord of Sirius (the star which the pagan Arabs used to worship).

trs.20: And that He destroyed the first [people of] ʿAad.
trs.85: that it was He who destroyed, in their entirety, ancient 'Ad
trs.22: And that it is He Who destroyed the (powerful) ancient 'Ad (people),
trs.203: And that it is He (Allâh) Who destroyed the former ‘Âd (people),

trs.20: And Thamūd - and He did not spare [them] -
trs.85: and Thamud,
trs.22: And the Thamud nor gave them a lease of perpetual life.
trs.203: And Thamûd (people): He spared none of them.

verses.text_uthmani: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَىٰ

trs.20: And the people of Noah before. Indeed, it was they who were [even] more unjust and oppressing.
trs.85: and before them the people of Noah who were even more unjust and insolent;
trs.22: And before them, the people of Noah, for that they were (all) most unjust and most insolent transgressors,
trs.203: And the people of Nûh (Noah) aforetime. Verily, they were more unjust and more rebellious and transgressing [in disobeying Allâh and His Messenger Nûh (Noah) عليه السلام].

trs.20: And the overturned towns<sup foot_note=197450>1</sup> He hurled down.
trs.85: that it was He who brought down the ruined cities
trs.22: And He destroyed the Overthrown Cities (of Sodom and Gomorrah).
trs.203: And He destroyed the overthrown cities [of Sodom to which Prophet Lût (Lot) was sent].

trs.20: And covered them by that which He covered.<sup foot_note=197451>1</sup>
trs.85: and enveloped them in the punishment He ordained for them?
trs.22: So that (ruins unknown) have covered them up.
trs.203: So there covered them that which did cover (i.e. torment with stones).

trs.20: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt?
trs.85: Which then of your Lord’s blessings do you deny?
trs.22: Then which of the gifts of thy Lord, (O man,) wilt thou dispute about?
trs.203: Then which of the Graces of your Lord (O man!) will you doubt?

trs.20: This [Prophet (ﷺ)] is a warner from [i.e., like] the former warners.
trs.85: This is a warning just like the warnings sent in former times.
trs.22: This is a Warner, of the (series of) Warners of old!
trs.203: This (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) is a warner (Messenger) of the (series of) warners (Messengers) of old.<sup foot_note=154952>1</sup>

trs.20: The Approaching Day has approached.
trs.85: The imminent Hour draws near
trs.22: The (Judgment) ever approaching draws nigh:
trs.203: The Day of Resurrection draws near.

verses.text_uthmani: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ

trs.20: Of it, [from those] besides Allāh, there is no remover.
trs.85: and only God can disclose it.
trs.22: No (soul) but Allah can lay it bare.
trs.203: None besides Allâh can avert it (or advance it or delay it).

trs.20: Then at this statement do you wonder?
trs.85: Do you [people] marvel at this?
trs.22: Do ye then wonder at this recital?
trs.203: Do you then wonder at this recitation (the Qur’ân)?

trs.20: And you laugh and do not weep
trs.85: Why do you laugh instead of weeping?
trs.22: And will ye laugh and not weep,-
trs.203: And you laugh at it and weep not,

trs.20: While you are proudly sporting?<sup foot_note=197452>1</sup>
trs.85: Why do you pay no heed?
trs.22: Wasting your time in vanities?
trs.203: Wasting your (precious) lifetime in pastime and amusements (singing, etc.).

trs.20: So prostrate to Allāh and worship [Him].
trs.85: Bow down before God and worship.
trs.22: But fall ye down in prostration to Allah, and adore (Him)!
trs.203: So fall you down in prostration to Allâh and worship Him (Alone).
